# RadioGroup

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

forms · tier 1 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For one choice out of a few, all shown at once. For many options, a Select reads better; for two
to five short ones in a bar, a SegmentedControl. It is two parts: a group and its radios.

```tsx
import { RadioGroupItem, RadioGroupRoot } from 'topclassui/radio-group'
```

```tsx
<span id="plan-label">Plan</span>
<RadioGroupRoot aria-labelledby="plan-label" name="plan" defaultValue="pro">
  <RadioGroupItem value="free">Free</RadioGroupItem>
  <RadioGroupItem value="pro">Pro</RadioGroupItem>
  <RadioGroupItem value="team">Team</RadioGroupItem>
</RadioGroupRoot>
```

**A name is required on the group.** Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; the type refuses a
group with neither. No `<label htmlFor>` can name a group. Each radio is named by its own text:
it sits in a `<label>` with the radio, so the text names it in the server HTML and a click on the
text selects it. The radio is a `<button>` with `role="radio"`.

**The group carries the state.** `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` are strings. Your
handler runs first, with Base UI's details, so `details.cancel()` leaves the group as it was.
`name`, `form`, `required`, `disabled` and `readOnly` go on the group; each radio carries its
`value`, its text and, if it needs one, its own `disabled`.

**A Field's props spread onto the group** with `aria-labelledby` beside them: a Field's label
cannot name a group through `htmlFor`.

```tsx
export function PlanField(control: { id: string, name: string, required: boolean, 'aria-describedby': string, 'aria-invalid': boolean }) {
  return (
    <RadioGroupRoot {...control} aria-labelledby={`${control.id}-label`}>
      <RadioGroupItem value="free">Free</RadioGroupItem>
      <RadioGroupItem value="pro">Pro</RadioGroupItem>
    </RadioGroupRoot>
  )
}
```

**The keyboard.** Tab enters the group on the checked radio and leaves it on the next Tab. The
arrows move to the next radio and select it, skip a disabled one, and wrap at both ends. Under
an RTL `TopClassProvider`, ArrowRight goes to the radio before. Space selects. Enter does not, and
there is no Home or End (Base UI's). Before the page hydrates the radio of `value`, else of
`defaultValue`, is the one tab stop. A group with neither, or with a value no radio has, serves
it on the first enabled radio it finds among its children, where Base UI keeps it once hydrated;
a radio a component of yours renders is not found. A disabled radio is a disabled button, so it
leaves the tab order and the arrow order.

**The form.** With a `name`, each radio has a hidden radio input: the form sends `name=<value>`,
and nothing while no radio is checked. Before the page hydrates it sends the default.
**A form reset**, a reset button or a React 19 form action that settles brings the group back
to its `defaultValue` of the latest render, on screen and in the form, or to none checked; a
controlled group keeps its owner's value. A reset calls no `onValueChange`.

**`required`** blocks a submit while no radio is checked. Before the page hydrates the browser
sends the focus of a blocked submit to a hidden input, a box of 1 px.

**`invalid`** sets `aria-invalid` on the group: every circle turns red and its line thickens,
checked or not. **`disabled`** is the real attribute on every radio, so the form sends nothing.
**`readOnly`** keeps the value in the form and sets `aria-readonly` on the group, which Chromium does
not announce; it has no look of its own either, so say it in the text beside the group.

**`orientation`** is `vertical` (a column) or `horizontal` (a row that wraps). It is layout only:
the arrows are the same in both.

**The target is 24 px, 44 px under a finger**, whatever `size` draws: the focus ring is around
the circle. Checked draws a line 2 px thick and the dot; the fill does not change. A long text
wraps under itself rather than ending in an ellipsis: a choice is read whole.

**On the item**, `className` and `style` go to the `<label>`; `ref`, `id` and the rest go to the
radio button. On the group they go to the `radiogroup`.

### What Base UI gives

| Base UI | Here |
|---|---|
| `RadioGroup`, `Radio.Root`, `Radio.Indicator`, `role="radiogroup"`, the arrows, Space | as they are |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` with `details.cancel()` | the same names, as strings; the value is held for the form reset |
| `name`, `form`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `inputRef` | passed through |
| a radio's `disabled`, `readOnly`, `inputRef` | passed through |
| a `<span>` radio, every radio `tabindex="-1"` in the server HTML | a native `<button>`, and one tab stop in the server HTML |

### Not built

`tone` (one is drawn), `RadioCards` (its own catalog row), a group that takes `items`, a
description under a radio's text, Home and End, a hover look, a read-only look, the invalid ring
that is always on, a skeleton (use `Skeleton`).

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import {
  RadioGroupRoot,
  RadioGroupItem,
} from 'topclassui/radio-group'
```

## Props

Required: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on `RadioGroupRoot`, `value` on `RadioGroupItem`. Every other prop below is optional.

### RadioGroupRoot

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | **yes**, or `aria-labelledby` | `string` | - | The name read out when no visible text names the group. |
| `aria-labelledby` | **yes**, or `aria-label` | `string` | - | The id of the visible text that names the group. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | `false` | RadioGroupRoot: marks the choice as wrong: sets aria-invalid on the group, and every circle turns to danger and thickens. |
| `orientation` | no | `vertical` \| `horizontal` | `"vertical"` | RadioGroupRoot: a column, or a row that wraps. Layout only, written as data-orientation; the arrow keys do not change. |
| `ref` | no | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | - | The element with role="radiogroup". |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | RadioGroupRoot: the toggle scale of every circle and the type step of its label; custom emits no size classes. |

### RadioGroupItem

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | **yes** | `string` | - | The string the form receives, and what `value` and `onValueChange` of the group carry. |
| `ref` | no | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | - | The radio itself, which is a `<button>`. |
| `style` | no | `CSSProperties` | - | On the `<label>` around the radio and its text. |

Anything else is passed to the element each part draws, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
